From 137ce13f74239ba3dc100269cafe842a1f4ea11d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Eran Mizrahi <eranmizra@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Apr 2011 21:10:37 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] RTL: Fix handling of special unicode marker 0xFEFF

This fixes a problem
in which the 0xFEFF mark was wrongly handled as RTL.

Change-Id: Icf8fce91e6df8c4fa8e01eb893174a9fdb8c0766

diff --git a/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java b/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java
index 88f725945..54bb57f0a 100644
--- a/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java
+++ b/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java
@@ -1692,7 +1692,7 @@ public class TextUtils {
                (c >= 0xFB1D && c <= 0xFB4F) ||
                (c >= 0x0600 && c <= 0x07BF) ||
                (c >= 0xFB50 && c <= 0xFDFF) ||
-               (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFF)    ;
+               (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFE)    ;
     }
 
     /**
-- 
2.48.1

## Summary

**File Modified:** `core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java`

**Modification:** Changed the upper bound of a Unicode range check used to determine right-to-left (RTL) characters. The range `0xFE70` to `0xFEFF` was narrowed to `0xFE70` to `0xFEFE`, excluding the character `0xFEFF` (the Zero Width No-Break Space / Byte Order Mark) from being classified as an RTL character.

**Relationship:** This is a single-file, single-line fix. The change directly addresses the bug described in the commit message: the special Unicode marker `0xFEFF` was being incorrectly included in the RTL character range check, causing it to be wrongly treated as an RTL character. By excluding `0xFEFF` from the range (changing `<= 0xFEFF` to `<= 0xFEFE`), the fix ensures this marker character is no longer misclassified, correcting the RTL detection logic used elsewhere in the codebase that depends on this method.

Here is the commit message:
RTL: Fix handling of special unicode marker 0xFEFF

This fixes a problem
in which the 0xFEFF mark was wrongly handled as RTL.

Change-Id: Icf8fce91e6df8c4fa8e01eb893174a9fdb8c0766

Here is the root cause:
The method responsible for detecting right-to-left (RTL) characters used an inclusive range check `(c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFF)` to identify characters belonging to Arabic Presentation Forms-B, a Unicode block containing RTL characters. However, this range incorrectly included the code point `0xFEFF`, which is not an actual RTL script character but a special Unicode formatting character (Zero Width No-Break Space, also used as a Byte Order Mark). Since `0xFEFF` falls at the very edge of the Arabic Presentation Forms-B block numerically but is semantically unrelated to RTL text directionality, the overly broad boundary condition caused this marker to be wrongly classified as RTL, leading to incorrect text direction handling wherever this character appeared.

Here is the patch:
 
     public static boolean isRTLCharacter(char c) {
         //range of RTL characters per unicode specification
         return (c >= 0x0590 && c <= 0x05FF) ||
                (c >= 0xFB1D && c <= 0xFB4F) ||
                (c >= 0x0600 && c <= 0x07BF) ||
                (c >= 0xFB50 && c <= 0xFDFF) ||
-               (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFF)    ;
+               (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFE)    ;
     }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
`(c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFF)`
Reason:
This boundary check treats the upper bound of the range as inclusive of `0xFEFF`, which is meant to capture the Arabic Presentation Forms-B Unicode block. However, `0xFEFF` is not an RTL script character—it is the Zero Width No-Break Space / Byte Order Mark, a formatting character. Because the range check does not exclude this special code point, any occurrence of `0xFEFF` in text is incorrectly classified as RTL, causing wrong text direction handling whenever this marker appears.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
`(c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFE)`
Reason:
By changing the upper bound from `0xFEFF` to `0xFEFE`, the range now correctly excludes the special Unicode marker `0xFEFF` while still covering all actual RTL characters in the Arabic Presentation Forms-B block (which ends at `0xFEFE` for genuine RTL characters). This ensures that `0xFEFF` is no longer misclassified as RTL, resolving the incorrect text direction handling.
